conflicts.fact: Sign and direction of the string error: whether 88 cm is longer or shorter than the exact circumference 28π
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 Observed/Explained says the string is about 0.035 cm longer than 28π (88 − 28π > 0, overlap). Lesson 7's Model Building step has an internal contradiction: it writes the gap as 28π − 88 and says '28π > 88 is FALSE'. Lesson 8 writes the error as |28π − 88| ≈ 0.035 cm. Since 28π ≈ 87.965 < 88, Lesson 7's primary claim is right and the Model Building text and Lesson 8's expression are in the wrong order.

conflicts.fact: Whether 22/7 is rational/irrational and its decimal expansion versus π; also the claim that rounding makes the answer 'exactly writable'
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 lists 22/7 = 3.142857… and treats it as rational, distinct from π. Lesson 1 leaves open whether 22/7 equals π. Lesson 5 says rounding to 88 or using 22/7 makes the answer rational and writable exactly, consistent with Lesson 3. No contradiction on this point, but Lesson 6 uses 3.142 as the approximation while the sufuria problem in other lessons uses 88 or 22/7. Not a conflict on facts.

conflicts.fact: Structure of the number system hierarchy and which sets are included
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2: ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℝ with irrationals (no whole numbers set), and Lesson 2 card list has 'Zero' separately. Lesson 4 says nested sets Natural → Whole → Integer → Rational → Real. Lesson 8 says Natural ⊂ Whole ⊂ Integer ⊂ Rational, with 'five number sets'. Lesson 2 requires five labelled regions (ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, Irrationals, ℝ) but Lessons 4 and 8 include Whole numbers as another set.

conflicts.fact: What the cumulative model contained from earlier lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says that in Lesson 1 learners drew the outer set 'Real Numbers' and in Lesson 2 added a number line, and Lesson 3 adds two non-overlapping rational/irrational subsets. Lesson 1 actually has a blob of 'All the numbers I know' with 10 numbers, and Lesson 2 has a full nested Venn diagram (ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, irrationals, ℝ), not a number line. Lesson 4 says the model started in Lesson 1 shows nested sets, which matches Lesson 2 rather than Lesson 3.

conflicts.fact: Kericho temperature dataset and Lesson 4's Kericho dataset
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4's Kericho record is seven daily temperatures (18, 19.5, √5 above baseline, 20, 18.75, 21, 19.333…°C), all positive. Lesson 8 uses 14 values (morning lows and afternoon highs) including −3.5°C, 2°C, 19°C, 24°C, 1°C, 28°C. A different dataset is used for the same Kericho phenomenon.

conflicts.fact: Classification of −3.5°C Kericho value and integer example
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8's model lists as an Integer example '−3.5°C Kericho morning rounded to −4' while elsewhere −3.5 is a rational non-integer; also the Natural example '28 cm diameter' is consistent. Minor oddity in Lesson 8 only.

Lesson 1: 1/3 is 'fraction of a githeri portion'. Lesson 2: 2/3 as fraction of a sufuria of githeri and 0.333… as 'one-third kg of unga'. Lesson 3: 0.333… is 'one-third of a 3-litre cooking-oil bottle'. Different contexts for the same number.
Lessons 1–3 and 5 say Ksh 60.50 is the price of 1 kg of unga. Lesson 5 Section A says Ksh 60.50 for a 2 kg packet, and Lesson 6 says Ksh 60.50 per kg.

Lesson 6 says Lessons 1–5 were classifying and Lesson 6 is where operating begins, but Lesson 5 is already titled and described as operating on real numbers (BODMAS, closure rules). Lesson 6 overview also says Explain error on rounding π as 3.142 while Lesson 5's daughter rounds to 88 cm.
